prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Phoenix after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Phoenix for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but I don’t have live web access in this chat to pull current local phone numbers and up-to-the-minute reputation data. I can either (A) give you a curated list of Phoenix firms right now if you want me to look them up (I’ll need to run a web search), or (B) give immediate, concrete guidance on which kinds of firms to call plus a short scripted checklist and questions to use when you call. Which do you prefer?

If you want option B right away, here’s a practical plan you can use immediately to find and vet good personal injury lawyers in Phoenix and to decide which ones to call:

Where to find reputable Phoenix personal-injury lawyers
- Arizona State Bar Lawyer Referral Service (reliable for licensed local attorneys).
- Super Lawyers and Martindale‑Hubbell directories (look for AV/peer-reviewed or “Super Lawyer” ratings).
- Google Maps, Yelp, Avvo — read recent reviews and look for patterns (responsiveness, trial experience, settlement results).
- Local trial firms that advertise personal injury / car-accident work and have trial verdicts or documented large settlements.

What types of firms to prioritize
- Plaintiff-side personal injury specialists (not insurance defense).
- Trial‑ready firms with experience taking cases to jury if needed (look for stated trial verdicts).
- Firms that handle auto accidents, catastrophic injuries, wrongful death, and uninsured/underinsured motorist claims if relevant.
- Firms that work on contingency (no fee unless they recover money).

Who to call first
- 3–5 firms: at least one large national/regional firm (may have resources), at least one mid-size firm with local trial lawyers, and one small boutique firm with a partner who will handle your case directly.

What to ask on the first call (short script)
1. “Do you take car-accident/personal-injury cases on contingency?” (If yes, get the percentage or range.)
2. “Do you handle cases like mine (describe injury, fault questions, whether other driver uninsured)? How many similar cases have you handled?” 
3. “Have you taken any car-accident cases to trial? What were the results?” (Trial experience matters.)
4. “Who will handle my case day-to-day — a partner, associate, paralegal?” (Get names.)
5. “Do you advance costs for the case, and how are medical liens handled?” 
6. “What’s your typical timeline and communication method?” 
7. “Can I get a written fee agreement and a plain-English explanation of fees and costs?” 

What to have ready before/when you call
- Date/time/location of crash, police report number (if available), photos of damage/injuries, names of drivers/witnesses, insurance info, brief description of injuries and medical treatment received so far.

Red flags to avoid
- Firms that pressure you to sign immediately without explaining the retainer.
- Promises of an exact dollar amount up front.
- Poor responsiveness on the phone or unwillingness to put things in writing.

Immediate next steps I can do for you
- If you want, tell me your ZIP code or the Phoenix neighborhood where the crash happened and I’ll (with your permission) run a web search and return a curated list of 6–8 Phoenix personal injury firms to call, with one-line reasons (trial experience, client ratings, specialties). Or I can draft the exact script you can use on the phone or in email.

Which would you like me to do next?
